newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian army fights rebels with 25-year-old guns.
newsitem.headline: Colombian army fights rebels with 25-year-old guns.

text.p: Colombia's army is fighting Latin America's richest and best-equipped guerrillas with 25-year-old rifles, armed forces chief Gen. Harold Bedoya said on Thursday.
He said recent defence spending hikes had started to lift the army out of "poverty" but admitted that it was still impossible for the military to defend the entire country.

"We've begun to come out of our position of poverty. ... It's not that there are soldiers without rifles in Colombia but there are soldiers with 25-year-old rifles that jam when they're in combat," Bedoya told a session of Congress.

The no-nonsense commander said an effort was under way to replace soldiers' elderly German-made G-3 rifles with Israeli- manufactured Galils but he said years of budget neglect had left the military at a competitive disadvantage against the rebels.
Bedoya also said the army did not have sufficient funds to maintain its fleet of Brazilian-made Cascabel armoured cars and light tanks.

In the congressional debate, Conservative legislator Pablo Victoria said intelligence reports showed Colombia's estimated 12,000 Marxist guerrillas, waging a war against the state since the mid-1960s, had one walkie-talkie for every two fighters, compared to the army's one radio for every 10 soldiers.
He also highlighted other unconfirmed reports that the army had just 45 rifles for every 100 soldiers.
